from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Core Invariant: Counting Sides"
        lines = [
            "Consider the points on each side of the line.",
            "Color points on the left red and right blue.",
            "As the pivot swaps, a point moves through the pivot.",
            "Crucially, the number of points on each side stays constant.",
            "This invariant is the key to solving the problem."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_LEFT = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan label
        COLOR_RIGHT = "#FF00FF" # Magenta label
        COLOR_RED = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_BLUE = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_LINE = "#FFFFFF"

        # Points
        # Pivot initially at C3
        pivot_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        left_points_pos = [self.grid["A2"], self.grid["B2"], self.grid["D2"], self.grid["E2"]]
        right_points_pos = [self.grid["A4"], self.grid["B4"], self.grid["D4"], self.grid["E4"]]
        
        all_points = VGroup()
        pivot_dot = Dot(pivot_pos, color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        left_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(p, color=WHITE, radius=0.08) for p in left_points_pos])
        right_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(p, color=WHITE, radius=0.08) for p in right_points_pos])
        all_points.add(pivot_dot, *left_dots, *right_dots)

        # Labels
        left_label = Text("4", font_size=36, color=COLOR_LEFT)
        self.place_at_grid(left_label, "C1")
        right_label = Text("4", font_size=36, color=COLOR_RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(right_label, "C5")

        # Line
        # We'll use a line that rotates. We need to handle pivot swaps.
        line_angle = ValueTracker(PI/2) # Start vertical
        line_pivot = ValueTracker(pivot_pos)

        def get_line_func():
            angle = line_angle.get_value()
            p = line_pivot.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            return Line(p - direction * 4, p + direction * 4, color=COLOR_LINE, stroke_width=2)

        rotating_line = always_redraw(get_line_func)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Consider the points on each side of the line.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(all_points)
        self.play(Create(rotating_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color points on the left red and right blue.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            left_dots.animate.set_color(COLOR_RED),
            right_dots.animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE),
            Write(left_label),
            Write(right_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # As the pivot swaps, a point moves through the pivot.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculate angle to B2 from C3.
        target_point = self.grid["B2"]
        diff = target_point - pivot_pos
        target_angle = np.arctan2(diff[1], diff[0])
        
        # Rotate line to the point
        self.play(line_angle.animate.set_value(target_angle), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Swap logic: C3 moves to the "right" side (blue), B2 becomes pivot (white)
        self.play(
            line_pivot.animate.set_value(target_point),
            pivot_dot.animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE),
            left_dots[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=0.1
        )
        
        # Continue rotation to show it passed
        self.play(line_angle.animate.set_value(target_angle - 0.3), run_time=1, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Crucially, the number of points on each side stays constant.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Flash(left_label, color=COLOR_LEFT, flash_radius=0.5),
            Flash(right_label, color=COLOR_RIGHT, flash_radius=0.5),
            left_label.animate.scale(1.2),
            right_label.animate.scale(1.2)
        )
        self.play(
            left_label.animate.scale(1/1.2),
            right_label.animate.scale(1/1.2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This invariant is the key to solving the problem.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(line_angle.animate.set_value(target_angle - 1.0), run_time=2, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(2)
